workflows.title: Full Task Lifecycle (goal → deliver)
workflows.body:
The master workflow. Every GENESIS job follows it.

1. **INTAKE** — Receive goal (P-01), constraints (P-06), budget (P-07).
   Exit: goal is concrete and verifiable; otherwise ask one clarifying question.
2. **RESEARCH** — Consult memory (P-03); gather external facts if needed.
   Exit: plan inputs collected or declared unavailable.
3. **PLAN** — Decompose into steps, each with expected state + verify method.
   Exit: written plan with per-step verification.
4. **EXECUTE** — Run the closed loop per step (T-01): observe → interpret →
   act → verify. Auto-recover small errors (T-10); escalate per gate class.
   Exit: all steps verified, or blocked with evidence.
5. **REVIEW** — Independent check against the goal (our LAW-050 merciless
   review): does the result match "done means"? Exit: PASS or fix-list.
6. **DELIVER** — Result + proof artifact (P-02) + spend report (P-07) +
   confirmed learnings to memory (P-04). Exit: father sees only the finished
   outcome.

workflows.title: Always-On Agent (Dots pattern, for scheduler)
workflows.body:
The long-lived background agent design, modeled on the public "Dots" product
pattern (Sept 29, 2026):

1. **CHARTER** — The father gives a standing goal + boundaries + approval
   classes (P-06). Stored, versioned, reviewable.
2. **BACKGROUND WORK** — The agent works between conversations on its own
   cloud/pc resources, following W-01 per sub-task.
3. **PROACTIVE REPORT** — Milestones and surprises are reported out (P-10);
   the agent may reach out first with a question or a decision needing a human.
4. **APPROVAL GATE** — Irreversible steps pause for father sign-off. Waiting
   is a first-class state with a clear resume path.
5. **PREFERENCE LEARNING** — Corrections update the preference record (P-09);
   the agent gets better at the father's taste without retraining.
6. **AUDIT** — Every action is logged with timestamp and evidence; the father
   (or an overseer) can inspect what the agent did, not just what it claims.

---

## Failure modes each workflow guards against

| Workflow | Primary failure mode | Guard |
|---|---|---|
| W-01 | Silent drift across steps | Per-step verify (T-01) |
| W-02 | Fixing symptoms, storing guesses | Reproduce-first + confirm-only storage |
| W-03 | Confident errors in drafts | Hostile self-QA pass |
| W-04 | Vendor hype treated as fact | Independent-confirmation rule |
| W-05 | Rogue autonomy | Approval gates + audit log + bounded charter |

workflows.title: Script → Avatar Video Pipeline (the master build flow)
workflows.body:
Owner: avatar host (+ scheduler for async render jobs).

1. **INTAKE** — Receive final script + identity reference + target spec
   (dimensions, language, quality tier). Exit: script locked; P-04 lexicon
   extracted. *Guard:* an unlocked script never enters the render queue.
2. **SCENE SPLIT** — Apply P-02: one concept per scene, emit the declarative
   manifest (video_inputs[]). Exit: manifest validates against schema.
   *Guard:* scenes with two concepts are split automatically or bounced.
3. **DRAFT RENDER** — P-06 draft tier; voice produced, sync re-rendered via
   T-02. Exit: draft MP4 exists. *Guard:* render timeout → job retries once,
   then escalates with the last log.
4. **PREVIEW QC** — P-09 checklist at full size: plosives, fingers, skin,
   pacing, pronunciation. Exit: clean pass or a fix-list. *Guard:* any
   failure routes to step 5, never to publish.
5. **FIX LOOP** — Fix inputs (lexicon, script line, background), reprocess
   (same seed where applicable). Max 3 rounds. Exit: QC pass or escalation
   to a human reviewer with the evidence. *Guard:* round 4 is forbidden;
   escalation is mandatory.
6. **FINAL RENDER** — Precision tier (T-07). Exit: final MP4 + checksum.
   *Guard:* checksum recorded; a final render without a passing draft QC is
   rejected by the gate.
7. **PUBLISH** — Deliver file + manifest + QC evidence. Exit: asset in the
   registry (T-09 identity reuse).

techniques.title: Declarative Studio API (video as data)
techniques.what_it_does: Videos are created through a declarative JSON manifest: an array of scenes, each specifying script text, avatar (id + style: rectangular / circular / voice-only), avatar settings (alignment, scale), and background (solid color, image, or green-screen for downstream replacement). A template endpoint accepts a template id plus template data and an optional brand-kit id. Script variables enable personalization (variables may not begin with a number). Generation is asynchronous: submit → poll status → retrieve finished file. Voices support SSML for pronunciation control.
techniques.why_it_works: A video becomes data: composable, version-controlled, machine-generatable. Templates + variables turn one master into thousands of personalized variants. Compare with HeyGen's declarative manifest — the Synthesia-specific patterns are script-variable personalization, the template+brandKitId endpoint shape, and SSML voice control.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Adopt a declarative scene manifest as the contract between the report module (which authors scripts) and the avatar host (which renders). Keep generation async with a status poller so long renders never block the scheduler. Variable naming rules and SSML-style pronunciation tags belong in the schema spec, not in tribal knowledge.

techniques.title: Living-Document Version Control (edit once, propagate everywhere)
techniques.what_it_does: Videos are not frozen files — they are living documents. Edit the master and every published copy updates automatically: shared links, website embeds, and LMS-delivered SCORM packages. Version history and analytics (views, completion, per-language comparison) attach to the document, not to a file.
techniques.why_it_works: It eliminates the version-drift problem that makes video programs expensive: a correction no longer means tracking down and replacing every copy in circulation. This is the defining "video *program*" feature versus a "make a video" tool.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Every GENESIS-produced video artifact should carry a master-id; derived copies (embeds, translations, LMS packages) are renders of the master, not independent files. A master edit triggers re-render of dependents with a change log. This is the single most program-grade pattern in the pack — adopt it as a platform-wide artifact convention, not just for avatar video.

techniques.title: Shared-Credit Metering (one pool, honest prices)
techniques.what_it_does: All AI features draw from one shared credit pool on each plan. Surface estimated spend in the job's pre-execution report. This fits our zero-spend discipline: costs are visible *before* the job runs.

techniques.title: Content-Moderation Render Gate (every video, before delivery)
techniques.what_it_does: Every generated video passes through content moderation before delivery. Scripts are held to professional/business standards — political, sexual, personal, criminal and discriminatory content are refused. Independent testers report render times of ~4–5 minutes for a short video, noticeably slower than HeyGen's ~1 minute, with the moderation step as a contributing factor.
techniques.why_it_works: For enterprise scale, trust is a feature. The moderation gate converts a brand-risk problem into a workflow step, and the render latency is the honest price of it. It also explains the platform's design posture: slower but governance-grade, versus HeyGen's faster but looser.
techniques.genesis_implementation: The publish governor (our breaking-news-style gate) should include a moderation stage for any generated media: script policy check → render → automated anomaly check → human review queue for flagged items. Accept explicit render latency for governed paths; keep a separate draft tier with lighter checks for internal previews.

- **What it does:** Every generated video passes through content moderation

workflows.title: Template/API Batch Production (one design, many variants)
workflows.body:
For personalized or series output at scale.

1. **DEFINE TEMPLATE** — Lock the scene manifest template: layout, avatar,
   brand kit, and script with named variables (P-05). A template id is
   minted. Entry: one approved example render. Exit: template passes a
   fallback-reading test (every fallback sounds natural spoken aloud).
2. **SET VARIABLES** — The data table: one row per output, columns for
   every variable. Entry: template id. Exit: table validated — no empty
   cells without declared fallbacks, no variable names starting with a
   number.
3. **BATCH SUBMIT** — Submit jobs asynchronously through the declarative
   API (T-08), with per-job credit estimates from the shared pool (T-11).
   Exit: all jobs accepted; any rejected submission is reported with its
   reason, never silently dropped.
4. **POLL** — Status poller tracks every job; completed renders are
   hashed and stored with their variable row. Exit: N submitted = N
   accounted (rendered or failed-with-reason) — arithmetic reconciliation.
5. **DISTRIBUTE** — Deliver per-row: link/embed/package. Analytics attach
   to the template id for aggregate comparison.
   Exit: distribution list with per-output delivery proof.

**Guarded failure modes:** budget overrun mid-batch → pause at the next
job boundary, report spend, resume only on approval; variable substitution
breaks pronunciation → the row is re-rendered from the correction queue,
not shipped as-is; template changed mid-batch → in-flight jobs finish on
the old template, new jobs take the new one, versions never mixed.

workflows.title: Living Video Maintenance (the program, not the file)
workflows.body:
The workflow that keeps a video library current after publishing.

1. **EDIT** — A detail changes: edit the master text/manifest.
   Entry: change request with the exact new wording.
   Exit: master amended with a change-log entry.
2. **RE-RENDER** — Affected scenes re-render; dependents (translations,
   dubs, variants) re-triggered per T-09.
   Exit: new master hash + per-dependent render status.
3. **AUTO-PROPAGATE** — Shared links, embeds, and LMS packages update to
   the new version automatically.
   Exit: propagation receipt per channel (N channels in = N updated).
4. **ANALYZE** — Built-in analytics: views, completion, per-language and
   per-version comparison.
   Exit: a short read-out: what viewers finished, where they dropped.
5. **ITERATE** — Low-completion segments feed back into a new EDIT cycle.
   Exit: next change request, or "holding — metrics healthy."

**Guarded failure modes:** propagation failure on one channel → the
channel is retried, then escalated; the master version is never rolled
back to hide it; a revoked identity (P-10) triggers re-render or
retirement of affected videos across all channels before the next
propagation cycle.

---

## Cross-workflow rules

- **No orphan renders:** every output references its master id. A render
  without a master is not shippable (composition rule, Master-Script-First).
- **Arithmetic honesty:** batch and localization runs reconcile counts
  (submitted = rendered + failed-with-reason); propagation reconciles
  channels (in = updated). Unreconciled numbers never reach the father.
- **Independent re-review:** any capability the workflow newly depends on
  (a new engine version, a new language pair) passes our merciless review
  (LAW-050) before production use — the ARC-AGI-3 lesson.
- **Voice guardrail:** workflows W-01/W-02/W-03 include voice-synthesis
  stages as GENESIS product capability. The 369 publish path runs the same
  workflows with voice stages disabled — the NO AI VOICE LAW is enforced
  at the gate, not by trust.

techniques.title: Pronunciation Dictionaries + SSML Pause Control
techniques.what_it_does: A custom pronunciation dictionary maps problem words (names, acronyms, serial numbers, brand terms) to phonetic spellings; SSML `<break time="1.5s"/>` gives precise pause control between sentences. techniques.why_it_works: The model guesses pronunciation from orthography; the dictionary overrides the guess with certainty. Explicit pause tags beat punctuation for timing.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Voice module keeps a persistent pronunciation dictionary (seeded with the father's name, project names, "369", "GENESIS") applied automatically to every render. workflows.title: TTS Production Pipeline (script → finished audio)
workflows.body:
The pipeline for any non-conversational speech (briefings, narration,
announcements).

1. **INTAKE** — Text + intent (narration / announcement) + target voice.
   Exit: script + intent + voice_id, all present.
2. **NORMALIZE (P-01)** — Expand acronyms/numbers, strip URLs, spell out
   everything to be spoken. Exit: script reads aloud cleanly by a human.
3. **PRE-FLIGHT (P-05)** — Scan for acronyms, names, numbers, brand terms;
   resolve through the pronunciation dictionary. Exit: zero un-resolved
   tokens.
4. **CHUNK (P-03)** — Split at paragraph/sentence boundaries; attach
   context hints (previous_text / next_text); write chunk manifest.
   Exit: chunks + manifest.
5. **RENDER** — Generate each chunk with the intent preset (P-04),
   direction tags (P-02), tier chosen by job (T-13). High-stakes jobs:
   three-take selection (P-07). Exit: all chunks rendered with manifests.
6. **STITCH + QC** — Concatenate with cross-fades at joins; QC checks:
   embedding distance across joins (drift), tag adherence, no artefacts,
   pauses natural. Re-render only failing paragraphs and splice.
   Exit: single audio file passing all QC checks.
7. **SEAL (P-08)** — Watermark + provenance log. Exit: provenance record
   complete; audio is marked synthetic and is rejected by the 369 publish
   gate.

Failure modes guarded:
| Failure | Guard |
|---|---|
| Mispronounced acronym/serial | Pre-flight dictionary, not post-listen |
| Voice drift across chunks | Context hints + embedding-distance QC |
| Flat delivery over long scripts | Chunking ≤ ~200 words per pass + direction tags |
| Unlabeled synthetic audio leaking | Watermark-and-log is a mandatory stage, not optional |

workflows.title: TTS Production Pipeline (script → finished audio)
workflows.body:
The pipeline for any non-conversational speech (briefings, announcements,
narrations for the father).

1. **INTAKE** — Text + intent (briefing / announcement) + target voice_id
   + direction note. Entry: voice has a valid P-07 provenance header.
   Exit: intake accepted, or rejected (missing provenance = no render).
2. **NORMALIZE** — P-08 + P-01: strip unpronounceable content, expand
   numbers/acronyms, compute input byte count and cost estimate. Entry:
   intake accepted. Exit: render-ready script + byte cost, or escalation
   if over budget.
3. **DIRECT** — Compile direction (P-02 tags / P-03 director's note) onto
   the normalized script. Entry: render-ready script. Exit: directed
   script with inspectable tag stream.
4. **RENDER** — Generate via the two-stage path (T-01/T-02): semantic plan
   then acoustic render, chunked streaming for long text. Entry: directed
   script. Exit: raw audio.
5. **ROUND-TRIP QC** — Automatic re-transcription (T-11): diff words and
   vocal instructions against the prompt. Check the triple rubric (T-10):
   semantic accuracy, acoustic quality, speaker similarity. Entry: raw
   audio. Exit: PASS → delivery; FAIL → W-02 returns to RENDER (with
   P-06 patch-one-word first), never to delivery.
6. **DELIVER** — Final audio to the requesting module. Entry: QC PASS.
   Exit: delivered with QC report attached (word-error delta, bytes in,
   seconds out, render cost).

Failure modes guarded:
| Failure | Guard |
|---|---|
| Synthetic audio reaches 369 content | Provenance tag checked at delivery; publish gate fails closed on synthetic |
| Mispronunciations / skipped words ship | Round-trip QC fails closed; patch-before-rerender keeps cost down |
| Cost surprise on long renders | Byte count + estimate reported at NORMALIZE, before render |
| Wrong emotion lands on the wrong word | Tag stream is inspectable at DIRECT; QC checks instruction adherence |

workflows.title: Concept-to-Video Pipeline (idea → finished clip)
workflows.body:
The master production workflow for a single video asset.

1. **BRIEF** — Write the brief in the nine-section schema (T-04), with the
   style manifest (P-07) and continuity non-negotiables (P-08) filled.
   Exit: brief is complete; a brief with an empty CONTINUITY section is
   rejected, not debated.
2. **ENGINE SELECT** — Choose primary engine + fallback order and record the
   cost tier (T-10); compute the estimated cost and attach it to the job
   (T-09).
   Exit: engine plan + cost estimate committed before any spend.
3. **HERO FRAME** — Generate/select the hero still (P-02).
   Exit: frame QC'd and locked (face/product/composition correct).
4. **GENERATE** — Animate via image-to-video with identity/motion split
   (P-01), camera preset token (P-03), anatomy/physics specs (P-05, P-06),
   audio spec (P-09).
   Exit: clip artifact on disk.
5. **QC** — Independent review against the brief: identity match, camera
   move correct, continuity holds, no anatomy artifacts, ≥3s text timing for
   overlays (REEL TEXT-TIMING LAW), anti-AI-slop check (LAW-149).
   Exit: PASS, or a scoped repair list (go to W-03), or engine-fallback (go to
   W-04).
6. **DELIVER** — Clip + hero frame + brief + pill log + spend report to the
   caller (369 content team or father review).

**Guarded failure modes:**
- Engine returns anatomy artifacts → repair lane (W-03) with preserve list,
  max 2 repair rounds; if still failing, fallback engine (W-04).
- Cost estimate exceeds authorized budget → STOP, report to father; never
  auto-escalate spend.
- QC fails 3 consecutive generations → escalate to human director with the
  three failed artifacts side by side; do not keep burning credits.

workflows.title: Character-Consistent Series (episode N of a series)
workflows.body:
For any series with a recurring persona (presenter, character, product line).

1. **PROFILE LOCK** — Identity profile exists (T-03) with multi-angle
   composite sheet (T-14), descriptor block, and palette HEXes; profile
   version recorded.
   Exit: profile ID + version, or STOP (never generate a series without one).
2. **STYLE LOCK** — Style manifest committed (P-07): background/accent HEX,
   lighting preset, texture word. Moodboard for locations/wardrobe (T-13).
   Exit: manifest artifact, versioned.
3. **STORYBOARD** — Shot-job assignments (P-04) for the episode: each shot
   has a job, time window, camera preset, identity reference.
   Exit: storyboard with per-shot jobs; no "whatever angle looks coolest"
   entries.
4. **GENERATE SHOTS** — Per W-01 stages 3–4, shot by shot. End frame of shot
   N becomes start frame of shot N+1 (T-08).
   Exit: all shot artifacts on disk.
5. **CROSS-EPISODE REVIEW** — Compare every shot against the ORIGINAL
   reference set (profile sheet + style manifest), NOT just the previous
   episode (T-08). Continuity non-negotiables (P-08) checked item by item.
   Exit: PASS all shots, or repair list scoped per shot (W-03).
6. **ASSEMBLE** — Stitch, grade to manifest, audio mix (P-09), export.
   Exit: finished episode + full provenance (profile version, manifest
   version, engine log).

**Guarded failure modes:**
- Face/outfit drift detected at step 5 → repair lane on the drifted shots
  only; if a repair alters identity, the profile is RE-versioned and the
  change is logged (identity never changes silently).
- A shot's hero frame fails lock → that shot does not enter generation;
  the pipeline continues with other shots (no blocked shots held as
  half-done).

workflows.title: Multi-Engine Fallback (shot routing)
workflows.body:
For shots that fail on the primary engine.

1. **DIAGNOSE** — Determine whether the failure is engine-mismatch
   (engine's known weakness, e.g. weak motion coherence) or prompt-mismatch.
   Exit: classified; only engine-mismatch proceeds here.
2. **ROUTE** — Select the next engine in the fallback order whose strength
   matches the shot's need (motion-heavy → motion-strong engine; realism →
   realism engine), keeping camera preset (P-03) and identity profile
   (P-01) identical.
   Exit: fallback engine selected, same control spec.
3. **REGENERATE** — Rerun with the identical prompt/controls on the new
   engine. Cost re-estimated and re-authorized (T-09).
   Exit: new artifact, or next fallback.
4. **COMPARE** — Side-by-side QC of the best artifacts from each engine.
   Exit: winner selected with reasons recorded (engine lesson stored as
   confirmed memory: "shot type X → engine Y").

**Guarded failure modes:**
- Fallback list exhausted (all engines tried) → escalate to human director
  with the comparison grid; do not loop back to engine 1 automatically.
- A fallback engine costs more than the authorized budget → STOP and ask;
  the router never upgrades spend on its own.

workflows.title: Budget-Gated Batch Run (volume production)
workflows.body:
For producing many clips (campaign variants, A/B sets, episode batches).

1. **BATCH PLAN** — Brief template (T-12) instantiated per variant; each
   variant gets an engine choice + cost estimate (T-10, T-09).
   Exit: batch manifest with per-variant cost and total cost.
2. **AUTHORIZE** — Total cost presented for approval (human or pre-authorized
   cap). Exit: explicit authorization; unauthorized = no generation.
3. **RENDER** — Variants render in priority order; spend is tracked against
   the manifest live. Exit: all artifacts, or spend cap hit.
4. **SPEND REPORT** — Actual vs. estimated cost per variant; lessons for
   future estimates (calibration data for T-09).
5. **ARCHIVE** — Artifacts + manifests + spend report stored; reusable
   template updated if the chain proved itself (T-12).

**Guarded failure modes:**
- Spend reaches 90% of cap mid-batch → pause, report, ask; never finish a
  batch by silently exceeding the cap.
- One variant fails repeatedly → quarantine it and continue the batch; a
  single bad variant never blocks the rest.
- Credit pricing changes mid-batch (vendor-side) → re-estimate remaining
  variants before continuing.

---

## Cross-cutting guardrails (all workflows)

- **No generation without a locked hero frame** (W-01 stage 3) for
  likeness-critical work.
- **No spend without a pre-generation cost disclosure** (T-09) — zero-spend
  discipline is enforced in the pipeline, not in policy text.
- **Continuity is checked against originals, never against the last output**
  (W-02 stage 5) — the anti-drift invariant.
- **Anti-AI-slop (LAW-149):** every workflow's QC stage includes the
  human-quality check — directed camera language, deliberate style manifest,
  no glossy-generic output. A clip that passes technical QC but looks like
  a thousand other AI clips FAILS and returns to repair.
- **Provenance:** every delivered artifact carries its profile version,
  style-manifest version, engine, pill log, and spend — arithmetic that
  reconciles (MATHEMATICAL PRECISION LAW).

techniques.title: Extend Chaining with a Hard Quality Ceiling
techniques.what_it_does: Extend adds 7-second hops to a clip (up to ~20 extensions, ~148s theoretical). Documented reality: quality degrades after 3–5 extensions (motion jitter, character drift); practical output is 30–60s.
techniques.why_it_works: Iterative continuation is the only way short-clip models make sequences — but drift compounds per hop, so the mechanism needs a ceiling.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Any chained-generation workflow must declare a max-hop limit (default: 4, ~32s) in the job schema. Exceeding it requires ingredients re-anchoring (T-01) and a QC checkpoint at each hop. Jobs that chain past the ceiling without checkpointing are rejected by the scheduler. This is the anti-drift guard our own reels need: no infinite extension.

workflows.title: Idea → Film Pipeline (the master sequence)
workflows.body:
The master workflow. Every video deliverable follows it.

1. **INTAKE** — Receive the brief: goal (what the film must do), constraints
   (budget, tier, models allowed), done-means (how QC judges it).
   Exit: concrete, verifiable goal; otherwise one clarifying question.
2. **PLAN AS SHOTS** — Break the idea into a shot list (P-06 coverage:
   establishing/medium/close-up). Each shot gets: the five-layer prompt
   (P-01), ingredients (P-03), camera token (P-07), audio spec (P-05).
   Exit: written shot list with per-shot locks; no locks, no render.
3. **LOCK THE LOOK** — Moodboard → variation set (P-10) → winning style
   ingredient (P-09). Exit: one locked moodboard attached to every shot.
4. **DRAFT CHEAP** — Render each shot at the lowest tier (T-07): composition
   and timing only. Exit: drafts approved for composition; identity defects
   are expected and ignored at this tier.
5. **RENDER HEROES** — Standard/hero tier only for shots whose drafts passed.
   Frame-lock (P-04) where composition is pre-decided. Exit: all hero clips
   rendered; failed ones fixed by masked edit (T-09) or re-rendered with a
   recorded reason.
6. **ASSEMBLE** — SceneBuilder-style timeline (T-04): arrange, trim, order;
   extend-chains (P-08) for sequences over ~32s with QC checkpoints.
   Exit: timed assembly; every on-screen text ≥3s (the reel law).
7. **AUDIO PASS** — Verify native audio per clip; repair the audio lane for
   extended/masked chains (T-05) — re-record or layer SFX as needed.
   Exit: full mix, no silent gaps, no desync.
8. **MERCILESS REVIEW** — Independent scored review (LAW-050), including the
   anti-AI-slop criterion (LAW-149): nothing generic, glossy, or formulaic
   passes. Exit: PASS or fix-list.
9. **DELIVER** — Export (MP4/WebM/frames), archive prompts + ingredients +
   settings into the prompt library (T-06 Flow TV pattern), spend report.
   Exit: father sees only the finished outcome.

Failure mode guarded: skipping locks (step 2–3) and going straight to render —
blocked by the pre-generation validator.

workflows.title: Agentic Batch Production (Flow Agent pattern, for scheduler)
workflows.body:
For producing many assets or variants unattended (T-14, Astra W-01/W-05).

1. **CHARTER** — Standing goal + boundaries + budget tier + approval classes
   (P-06 of Astra). Stored, versioned, reviewable.
2. **PLAN-AS-PACK** — The agent emits a storyboard/prompt pack: shot list,
   prompts, ingredients, tiers. Reviewable BEFORE any spend.
   Exit: pack approved (human or policy gate).
3. **QUEUED EXECUTION** — Renders run in the background per the pack; the
   agent watches, auto-recovers cheap failures, escalates per gate class.
   Exit: all pack items rendered or blocked with evidence.
4. **HOUSEKEEPING** — Files renamed by convention, media sorted into named
   collections, unused assets archived (T-13).
   Exit: collection tidy, register complete.
5. **PROACTIVE REPORT** — Milestones and surprises reported out; the father
   sees finished outcomes, not render logs.
   Exit: delivery + spend report + prompt-library updates.

Entry: approved charter. Exit: finished assets + tidy collection + report.
Failure mode guarded: silent spend and anonymous assets — blocked by the
pack-approval gate and the naming/collection rules.

workflows.title: Identity Onboarding (train once, reuse forever)
workflows.body:
- **Entry criteria:** 10–20 clear face photos (single subject, varied angles,
  good light); written consent for likeness use on file; target use declared
  (portrait series / video / template fills).
- **Steps:**
  1. Validate photo set (face detectable in all, no second person, mouth
     visible in ≥3).
  2. Train identity token (10–30 min class of job; tracked as a scheduled job
     with progress events).
  3. Verification pass: generate 4 test portraits across 2 styles; likeness
     score vs reference embedding ≥ threshold on all 4.
  4. Register identity: store token id, reference embedding, consent record,
     version number.
- **Exit criteria:** identity token registered with 4/4 likeness tests passing;
  consent record attached; cost logged.
- **Guarded failure modes:**
  - Photo set fails validation → return the failing photos with reasons;
    NEVER train on a weak set (a weak identity poisons everything downstream).
  - Likeness test < threshold → retrain with augmented set (more angles) or
    reject identity; never ship a "close enough" token.
  - Consent missing → job blocked at the gate; no override path.

workflows.title: Template-Driven Campaign (theme packs at volume)
workflows.body:
- **Entry criteria:** campaign brief (theme, count, platforms); template set
  approved by the format authority; identity tokens registered (or "no
  identity" declared for non-character pieces).
- **Steps:**
  1. Instantiate templates: each slot filled by P-08 (identity + ≤10-word
     scene keywords; text zones reserved, never AI-generated text).
  2. Batch generate (variant batches per slot, W-02 selection per slot).
  3. Series continuity pass: all pieces checked against the campaign manifest
     as a SET, not individually — the family must read as one.
  4. Bulk export at per-platform specs; registry updated with piece ids,
     templates, costs.
- **Exit criteria:** full set delivered at spec; set-level continuity passing;
  per-piece costs reconciled to campaign budget.
- **Guarded failure modes:**
  - One slot keeps failing → swap the template for that slot (templates are
    interchangeable by design) rather than burning credits on a bad fit.
  - Set-level continuity fails → identify the outlier piece(s); regenerate
    the outliers against the manifest, never "accept the set anyway."
  - AI-generated text appears in an image → piece rejected; text is rendered
    by the type system downstream, never by the generator (PERSIAN/typography
    laws apply to all on-piece text).

techniques.title: Quality Ladder (cost-aware draft → final)
techniques.what_it_does: The API exposes a quality ladder (low / medium / high, and higher tiers on newer models): drafts run cheap at low quality, exploration at medium, only the final asset at high. Cost per image scales roughly 10x per step up the ladder.

workflows.title: Draft→Final Cost Ladder (zero-spend enforcement)
workflows.body:
The economic discipline wrapping every image job.

1. **BUDGET** — Before any call: estimate calls × quality tier cost
   (T-08). Entry: the job's image count and tier plan. Exit: a written
   cost estimate attached to the job.
2. **DRAFT SWEEP** — Exploration at LOW quality only. Exit: chosen
   direction; all drafts logged with cost.
3. **CANDIDATE** — At most 2 medium-quality candidates. Exit: one sealed
   candidate or an escalation.
4. **SINGLE FINAL** — Exactly one HIGH-quality render of the sealed
   candidate. Exit: final asset.
5. **RECONCILE** — Actual spend vs. estimate; overruns named with cause.
   Exit: cost record stored with the job; patterns (e.g. "QC failures
   doubled spend") fed back to memory.

Failure modes guarded: flagship-priced drafts (tier enforced by stage),
silent spend (estimate before, reconcile after), iteration inflation
(W-02's circuit breaker caps the expensive tail).

workflows.title: Long-Horizon Initializer Chain (jobs that outlive one session)
workflows.body:
For work spanning many sessions (the Birth-Test shape).

1. **INITIALIZE** — First session is the initializer (T-12): writes the setup
   script, the progress file, the feature checklist (T-09: description +
   verification steps + pass flag per feature), and the baseline commit (T-11).
   Exit: artifacts exist; baseline is committable and clean.
2. **CHAIN** — Each subsequent session: reads the progress file + checklist,
   does ONE increment, updates the checklist, commits, exits clean.
   Exit: exactly one verified increment per session; working tree clean.
3. **MAINTAIN** — Context hygiene runs continuously (W-05): tool-result
   clearing, then compaction at threshold with the preserved-decisions
   template (T-08); instruction refresh when drift is detected (P-07).
   Exit: context stays under budget without losing decisions or open bugs.
4. **GATE** — No new feature starts while any checklist item is failing.
   Unverified claims never flip a flag (P-08).
   Exit: every flag is PASS with evidence, or the job is honestly blocked.
5. **HANDOVER** — Final session writes the completion record: what was built,
   what was verified, what remains. The next reader starts from artifacts,
   never from memory of a conversation.

workflows.title: Context Maintenance Cycle (keep the window high-signal)
workflows.body:
Runs continuously inside any long job; owned by the scheduler.

1. **CLEAR** — Continuously replace old tool-result bodies with placeholders;
   keep the tool-use record (lightweight, mechanical, zero inference).
   Exit: dominated-by-recallable-output bloat removed.
2. **NOTE** — Agent writes decisions, open bugs, and implementation details to
   the external notes/progress file as they happen (T-09).
   Exit: state exists outside the window.
3. **COMPACT** — At the token threshold, summarize and restart from the
   summary: goal, decisions, unresolved bugs, details, last verified state,
   recent files (T-08). Tune for recall first.
   Exit: restarted session, decisions and open bugs intact.
4. **VERIFY-CONTINUITY** — After compaction, the agent restates the goal and
   the next step from the summary; mismatch with the pre-compaction plan is a
   defect to fix before continuing.
   Exit: continuity confirmed, or summary corrected.

---

## Failure modes each workflow guards against

| Workflow | Primary failure mode | Guard |
|---|---|---|
| W-01 | Stale plan executed to failure; unverified steps | Interleaved reflection (T-02) + plan gate (T-10) + proof-required verify (P-08) |
| W-02 | Vendor hype or single-source claims treated as fact | Cross-check stage; confidence-graded findings table |
| W-03 | Author reviewing own work (blind to own flaws) | Clean-window reviewer; external Kiro/9Router gate in parallel |
| W-04 | Session-boundary amnesia; drifting "done" | Initializer artifacts; checklist gating; commit-per-increment |
| W-05 | Context rot (silent degradation as window fills) | Mechanical clearing → structured notes → recall-tuned compaction |

techniques.title: Effort-Tiered Agent Modes (Free / Power / Max)
techniques.what_it_does: Three effort tiers map to model capability and cost. Free Mode covers everyday builds and learning with no credit spend (plan-limited capacity, resets periodically). techniques.why_it_works: Not every task deserves flagship compute. Tiering makes the cost/quality tradeoff a deliberate per-task choice and gives users a clear escalation ladder (Free → Power → Max) instead of one price for everything.

techniques.title: Checkpoint Snapshots with Full Rollback
techniques.what_it_does: Every agent work unit is captured as a checkpoint that restores files, agent memory, task state, and optionally the development database. Rollback returns the whole project to any earlier checkpoint. Database recovery windows are plan-dependent (e.g., days of point-in-time restore on higher tiers).
techniques.why_it_works: Autonomous agents make wrong turns; without cheap undo, the operator is forced to let a runaway build continue or lose everything. A checkpoint converts "the agent ruined it" into a two-click recovery, which is what makes long unattended runs psychologically affordable.
techniques.genesis_implementation: In the hands + station modules, snapshot the workspace (file tree hash + job state + memory diff) before every mutation stage of an app build. Expose `rollback(checkpoint_id)` in the scheduler. Critical edge case learned from Replit postmortems: code rollback and data rollback are INDEPENDENT axes — restoring files does not restore data and vice versa, so GENESIS snapshots must cover both and the rollback UI must say which axes it restores.

techniques.title: Parallel Agent Forks + Bounded Autonomy Windows
techniques.what_it_does: The agent can fork parallel task streams (split work, combine results) — Core plans get two parallel agents, Pro gets ten. Agent v4 reportedly supports long autonomous runs (up to ~200 minutes) where it works through plan, test, and debug cycles without interruption.
techniques.why_it_works: Independent sub-tasks (frontend + backend, or two alternative implementations) parallelize cleanly; wall-clock time drops without quality loss. The time bound turns "autonomous" into a budgeted resource rather than an open-ended credit fire.
techniques.genesis_implementation: In the scheduler, support `parallel_forks` per job with a merge step, and give every unattended app-build run an explicit time/step budget (default short). A run that hits its budget stops with a status report — it never spins indefinitely. This is the defense against the documented "agent loops burning $350 in a day" failure class.

techniques.title: Lazy-Loaded Agent Skills (agentskills.io SKILL.md)
techniques.what_it_does: Skills are markdown instruction files in a project skills directory following an open standard. The agent sees every skill's name and description but loads the full content only when relevant to the current task. techniques.why_it_works: It solves context bloat: capabilities scale with the skill library without every skill consuming tokens on every task. Self-authoring closes the loop between doing and documenting.

techniques.title: Deployment-Type Selection (static / autoscale / reserved / scheduled)
techniques.what_it_does: Publishing is not one button but a choice of deployment types matched to workload: static sites, autoscale (traffic-variable apps), reserved VMs (continuous services), and scheduled jobs (cron-style runs). The builder picks the behavior, not just the code.
techniques.why_it_works: Hosting behavior is part of the product spec. Matching deployment type to workload prevents paying reserved-VM prices for a static landing page and prevents static hosting from choking a live app.
techniques.genesis_implementation: In the hands publish stage, require a declared deployment type per artifact with cost implications shown up front. For the father's use cases: landing pages → static; always-on agents/tools → reserved or scheduled. The scheduler's job schema carries `deploy_target`.

workflows.title: Plan Review Workflow (deliberation before mutation)
workflows.body:
For: architectural changes, multi-file refactors, anything touching data or
deployment config.

1. **DRAFT** — Agent produces the plan in Plan Mode: files to create/change,
   schema changes, design decisions, risks, and what will NOT change (T-02,
   P-03).
   Exit: plan document exists and is reviewable.
2. **TRIM** — Human (or Agent YZ) reviews: cut scope, resolve open decisions,
   lock the plan.
   Exit: approved plan with a locked hash; unapproved plan cannot proceed.
   Failure guard: no silent scope growth — any deviation during execution
   stops the job and returns to this step.
3. **EXECUTE** — Build Mode runs the locked plan with per-stage checkpoints
   (P-09).
   Exit: all plan steps verified.
   Failure guard: a step that would change something outside the locked plan
   is blocked by the permission gate and reported.
4. **RECONCILE** — Diff the result against the locked plan.
   Exit: every change is traceable to a plan line; nothing extra.
   Failure guard: untraceable changes are rolled back, not kept.

workflows.title: Staged Large Build (for projects beyond one sitting)
workflows.body:
For: builds too large for a single agent run (the failure class where long
sessions drift or loop).

1. **DECOMPOSE** — Split the spec into stages, each shippable and
   self-testable on its own (P-02 applied recursively).
   Exit: stage list with per-stage acceptance tests and dependencies.
   Failure guard: a stage whose acceptance test needs another stage's
   output is re-split — stages must be independently verifiable.
2. **STAGE RUN** — Run W-01 per stage, with a hard time/step budget per
   stage (T-08).
   Exit: stage passes its acceptance tests.
   Failure guard: budget exhausted → stage stops with a status report;
   never auto-continues. The human decides: extend, re-scope, or abandon.
3. **INTEGRATE** — After each stage, run the cross-stage user flow.
   Exit: the growing app still works end to end.
   Failure guard: integration breakage rolls back to the last integrated
   checkpoint (T-04) — never patch-forward on a broken base.
4. **COST CHECK** — After each stage, report cumulative effort/cost vs the
   job budget (T-14).
   Exit: spend on track; continue authorized.
   Failure guard: projected total exceeds 150% of budget → job pauses for
   father approval before the next stage.

techniques.title: Background Consolidation (Dreaming-style memory)
techniques.what_it_does: An offline background process periodically re-reads accumulated conversation history, synthesizes it into a living summary, revises outdated entries (a planned trip becomes a past event), merges duplicates, converts relative dates to absolute, and injects the synthesized state into new conversations' context.
techniques.why_it_works: Raw memory accumulates like a hoarder's attic: stale, contradictory, duplicated. Consolidation is the REM sleep of memory — it keeps the record current without the user curating it.
techniques.genesis_implementation: A scheduler cron (memory consolidation job): nightly sweep over explicit memories — mark stale by timestamp, contradiction-check new vs old, merge duplicates, rewrite relative dates. Confirmed-only rule (our T-06 from Astra): entries without a verified source event are candidates for deletion, never for promotion. Log every revision for audit.

techniques.title: Natural-Language Scheduled Tasks
techniques.what_it_does: Users describe a recurring task in plain words ("every Friday morning, run a health check-in with me"); the platform confirms the schedule it understood and asks for approval before it goes live. All tasks live in a task-hub page (add, pause, inspect next run). Plans cap active task counts; paid tiers get exact times and higher frequency; eligible plans add event triggers (Gmail/Slack/GitHub activity).
techniques.why_it_works: Natural-language scheduling removes cron syntax; the confirm-before-live step prevents misunderstood schedules from silently firing; the hub makes automation inspectable (automation you can't see is automation you can't trust).
techniques.genesis_implementation: The scheduler's job schema should accept schedule descriptions in Persian/English, parse to a canonical cron-like spec, and echo it back for confirmation before activation — no silent schedules, ever. A `tasks` listing (what runs, when next, pause/resume) must exist as a first-class view. Task counts per tier are fine, but our tier is the father only: log spend per task run.

techniques.what_it_does: Voice mode accepts spoken commands that trigger multi-step tasks (draft a doc, summarize messages), not just spoken Q&A. techniques.why_it_works: It exploits dead time (walking, driving) for task initiation and decouples input modality from execution — the task doesn't die when the call does.
techniques.genesis_implementation: The voice module should accept task-level commands ("draft X", "check Y"), hand a structured job to the scheduler, and let the father continue or inspect it in text. workflows.title: Custom Assistant Setup (Create → Configure → Preview → Save)
workflows.body:
Modeled on the public GPT Builder workflow. Builds a reusable assistant pack
(T-01).

1. **DESCRIBE** — Father states the job in plain words. The system drafts a
   pack: name, charter, instructions, capability needs. (P-01, P-02)
   Exit: a draft pack record exists with all fields filled.
2. **CONFIGURE** — Father (or an agent) edits the configuration directly:
   identity, instructions, knowledge bundle, tool allowlist + contracts,
   starters. (T-04, P-04)
   Exit: config is complete; every tool has a validated contract + behavior
   note; starters are all answerable.
3. **PREVIEW** — Run the pack's test script against realistic prompts,
   including edge cases and instruction conflicts, in a sandbox.
   Exit: all test prompts pass; no tool called outside its contract.
4. **SAVE** — Version, publish to the pack registry with visibility
   (private by default). Record charter version.
   Exit: versioned pack retrievable by name; audit entry written.
5. **REVIEW LOOP** — Corrections update the pack config (P-09-style
   preference learning), re-running PREVIEW before re-save.
   Exit: config and tests green again.

Guarded failure modes: aspirational starters (rejected at PREVIEW), unvalidated
tool contracts (blocked at CONFIGURE), silent visibility changes (all shares
logged).

workflows.title: Scheduled Task Automation Loop
workflows.body:
Standing automation with a human in the loop at creation.

1. **REQUEST** — Father describes the recurring task in natural language.
   Exit: a plain-words task description exists.
2. **PARSE + CONFIRM** — Scheduler parses to a canonical spec and echoes it
   back (P-10). No activation before the father's "yes".
   Exit: explicit confirmation recorded.
3. **RUN** — Each execution follows the full task lifecycle (verify per
   step; approval gates for irreversible actions). Failures are reported,
   not retried blindly.
   Exit: run log with evidence; blockers surfaced with the evidence.
4. **HUB** — The task appears in the task listing: schedule, next run,
   pause/resume, edit, delete. (T-09)
   Exit: every active task is inspectable in one view.
5. **AMEND** — Changes append to the goal (amend, never reset); re-plan
   from last verified state.
   Exit: amended schedule re-confirmed before it takes effect.

Guarded failure modes: misunderstood schedule firing silently (P-10 gate),
runaway retries (per-run attempt cap + blocker report), invisible
automation (HUB listing is mandatory).

workflows.title: Voice-First Capture-to-Done
workflows.body:
For hands-free task initiation (T-11, P-09).

1. **CAPTURE** — Father speaks a task command. Voice transcribes and parses
   intent.
   Exit: transcript + parsed intent exist.
2. **STRUCTURE** — Intent becomes a scheduler job with goal, constraints,
   budget. The written record (transcript + job id) is stored to memory
   immediately.
   Exit: job registered; text side can see it.
3. **EXECUTE** — Job runs in text (scheduler + hands). The voice call may
   end; the job continues independently.
   Exit: result or blocker with evidence.
4. **RESUME** — Father continues in text or a later voice call; the system
   presents status from the written record, never from voice memory alone.
   Exit: father confirms outcome or issues corrections (which update the
   job, W-03 amend rule).
5. **MODE CHECK** — After intent shifts (T-12): re-derive the conversational
   mode and adjust response strategy; log the transition.
   Exit: response strategy matches the current mode.

Guarded failure modes: task dies with the call (STRUCTURE decouples them),
voice-only state lost (written record is the source of truth), mode drift
(MODE CHECK detector).

## Failure modes each workflow guards against

| Workflow | Primary failure mode | Guard |
|---|---|---|
| W-01 | Untested assistant drifting in production | Preview gate with test script |
| W-02 | Stale/contradictory memory in long jobs | Nightly consolidation + handoff-wins rule |
| W-03 | Misunderstood schedule firing silently | Confirm-before-live + hub visibility |
| W-04 | Work lost when voice call ends | Written record as source of truth |
